headline: BEARISH
headline_tag: Weeks of losses push Bitcoin back under $60,000

action.title: CUT / defend tightly with a stop-loss
action.detail: Keep acquisition running but defend it tightly: the headline is BEARISH, Bitcoin is down about 5% in a week and about 25% in a month, it is back under $60,000, and the Rally watch drop window that opened on 11 November is still open. Put every acquisition campaign on a 30-day return stop-loss and pause the ones that miss it, trim spend aimed at active traders (they tend to leave before conditions improve), and move messaging toward stablecoins, safety and education, which also fits this week's wallet-theft headlines. Keep a reserve rather than cutting to zero; step acquisition back up only once price closes back above the 200-week average ($67,961) and then the 200-day average ($72,030). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

reasons: Down about 25% over 30 days and over 90 days; back under $60,000.
Price is about 20% under its 50-day average, 35 days in a row.
Fear & Greed is 13 (extreme fear), yet many still bet on a rise with borrowed money.
Price is about 12% under its 200-week average; long-term trend reads flat.
watch: Fear is extreme, yet a lot of people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, so another slip could force many of those bets closed and make the drop sharper. A close above $61,250 and then $67,961 (the 200-week average) would be the first sign the drop is easing; a close below $58,952 (the 30-day low) would deepen it.
analysis: Bottom line: the headline stays BEARISH and Bitcoin has slipped back under $60,000, so today calls for calm, safety-first messages and careful spending, not promotions. Short term, the picture is soft: Bitcoin, near $59,806, has closed under its 50-day average for 35 days in a row, sits about 20% below it and about 26% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 13 out of 100. Even in this fear, a lot of people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which can make a further dip sharper, and reports of new US tariffs (WSJ via PANews) plus a run of wallet thefts are nudging the mood down a little. A normal week lately swings about $2,957, so a close above $61,250 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $58,952 (the 30-day low) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer content fits better than offers.

The next month leans clearly down: price is about 25% lower than 30 days ago and about 25% lower than 90 days ago, and US Bitcoin and Ether funds saw about $728 million leave on 24 November (Pluang). News is softening that a little, as South Korea published its draft crypto law allowing licensed stablecoins and coin offerings, and Anchorage Digital plans a Bitcoin fund for early December (both via PANews). Bitcoin would have to win back $75,139 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. US inflation data (PCE) is due on 25 November and the Fed meets on 8 December; keep bigger campaign pushes until after a clear turn.

Long term, the picture is flat rather than down: the 200-day average is still rising (about 4% over 90 days), but price is about 17% under it, about 12% under its 200-week average and about 52% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track while Bitcoin closes above $72,030 (the 200-day average); $67,961 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has slipped under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. Slow structural steps continue, such as BlackRock's first tokenized cash fund in Hong Kong (PANews), but more weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and make keeping existing users the main use of budget.
